newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sampo leads Helsinki up, Raisio falls, Silja jumps.
newsitem.headline: Sampo leads Helsinki up, Raisio falls, Silja jumps.

text.p: * Finnish shares end higher as Sampo appeals on falling interest rates and Silja jumps on channel restructuring. Raisio falls as New York Times story suggests upcoming competition.
* Helsinki general index HEX +0.42 pct at 2139.1
* Volume 345 million markka, 20 percent in Sampo

Shares rose on Friday with trade turning lively in the afternoon after a dormant start, and with underlying strong sentiment reviving despite some nerves ahead of a U.S. Federal reserve meeting next week, brokers said.
Sampo was liveliest as brokers said falling interest rates boosted expectations of higher investment income for the group.
Silja jumped five markka to 37.00 on a late channel traffic announcement which was seen capping its losses in the UK.
Kemira set a new 53.20 life high on hopes its planned issue would pull a high price. Konecranes also set a new record on buying ahead of its results due next week, brokers said.

Raision Tehtaat fell sharply -- down nine markka or over three percent to 271.00 -- after a story in the New York Times said U.S. Campbell Soup would begin selling by mail-order frozen meals designed to reduce high blood pressure, cholesterol and diabetes.
Brokers in Helsinki were slightly mystified but some sources said this had been interpreted as a potential threat to Raisio's patented cholesterol-lowering Benecol margarine.
On the week, the HEX was just 0.42 percent higher.
Next week's Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting would be in focus, said brokers, as it would revive rate hike fears.
